title: Amana vs. Friedrich Dehumidifier (2026): Capacity or Pump?
dek: Amana gives you 50 pints for a big basement; Friedrich gives you a pump and a five-year sealed-system warranty at 35. Here's which trade-off fits your space.
description: Amana vs. Friedrich dehumidifier, compared: the 50-pint AMND501AW and pump-equipped 35-pint D35B1B on capacity, drainage, warranty, recall history and value.
intro: On paper, the **Amana vs. Friedrich dehumidifier** matchup is a trade-off rather than a tie. Amana's AMND501AW is a 50-pint, ENERGY STAR-certified unit that drains to a big bucket or a gravity hose. Friedrich's D35B1B is a smaller 35-pint, ENERGY STAR-certified unit with a built-in pump — and, like the rest of the Friedrich range, it carries a premium over mainstream dehumidifiers.

The two brands share no owner or factory, but they do share one piece of history: both names appear in the same 2021 CPSC recall of dehumidifiers made by New Widetech. Neither current model is affected. What's left to separate them is capacity versus drainage convenience, warranty length, the depth of independent data, and how much you value a specialist HVAC brand. Here's how they compare, point by point.
topPicksLead: For a large, damp basement with a drain nearby, the **Amana AMND501AW** is the better fit; choose the **Friedrich D35B1B** if you need a built-in pump and a five-year compressor warranty for a mid-size space.

products.name: Amana 50-Pint Portable Dehumidifier (AMND501AW)
pros: 50 pints a day for large, damp spaces
Three fan speeds and an adjustable humidistat
cons: No built-in pump on this version
No independent test data we could find
products.whyWeLoveIt: It’s the bigger machine of the two: a true 50-pint unit with simple electronic controls, a 24-hour timer and auto-restart that keeps a basement unit working after a storm knocks the power out. If there’s a floor drain nearby, it removes more water a day than the Friedrich.
products.performance: Amana lists 50 pints a day with three fan speeds (232, 196 and 160 CFM), ENERGY STAR certification and auto-defrost for cooler basements. Coverage figures are inconsistent across retailers — about 4,500 square feet on one listing, 150 on another — so size it as you would any 50-pint unit. It drains to the bucket or a gravity hose, so hands-off running needs a drain lower than the unit. We didn’t find any independent bench test of a current Amana dehumidifier, so performance is unconfirmed either way. More in our [Amana guide](/best/best-amana-dehumidifier/).

products.name: Friedrich 35-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump (D35B1B)
pros: Built-in pump with up to 15 feet of combined lift
Runs down to 41°F with auto defrost
cons: 35 pints a day, well short of the Amana
Costs a premium over mainstream units
Its prior-generation sibling scored lower on durability
products.whyWeLoveIt: Friedrich is a dedicated HVAC brand, and it backs this unit with a five-year warranty on the compressor and sealed system — the part that’s most expensive to fix. The pump is the other draw: it lets you put the unit where the moisture is rather than where the drain is.
products.performance: Friedrich rates it at 35 pints a day, with retailers typically listing coverage around 800–1,000 square feet, a digital control range of 30–90% humidity and a pump that can push water up to 15 feet vertically, horizontally or a combination of both. There’s a 16.2-pint bucket if you’d rather not use the pump. This generation switched to R-32 refrigerant, replacing the D35B1A. The brand’s prior-generation 50-pint D50BP scored well in one independent review for hygrometer accuracy and quiet running, but only middling marks for durability. See our [Friedrich guide](/best/best-friedrich-dehumidifier/) for the full lineup.

blocks.text: We don't run a test lab. We compared a current model from each brand using manufacturer specs, retailer listings, published warranty terms, independent reviews where they exist and the CPSC recall database. Where the numbers disagree between sources — as Amana's coverage claims do — we say so.

sections.heading: Capacity, pump and warranty: what each one buys

blocks.text: The spec sheets point in opposite directions. The Amana removes more water — 50 pints a day versus 35 — while the Friedrich adds a pump and charges a premium over mainstream units of either size. Beyond the pump, what that premium buys is brand positioning and, above all, warranty.

Amana offers a standard one-year limited warranty. Friedrich adds a **five-year limited warranty on the sealed refrigeration system** on top of one year of parts and labor. Compressor failures are the costliest dehumidifier repairs, so that extra coverage is real value — especially for a unit that runs all summer in a basement.

blocks.title: Do the math for your situation
blocks.text: If you'd replace rather than repair a failed unit, the Amana's mainstream pricing makes that an easier call. If you'd rather have one machine for many seasons and the backing to fix it, the Friedrich's warranty tips the scales.

Friedrich's prior-generation D50BP earned a strong overall score in one independent bench review, including excellent marks for hygrometer accuracy (within about a point of actual humidity) and quiet running. The catch was durability, which scored noticeably lower, with the reviewer pointing to a relatively high share of owner reports of reliability problems.

The current D35B1B is a newer generation and a smaller model, so treat that as brand history rather than a verdict on this unit. We found no comparable independent test of any current Amana dehumidifier. That doesn't mean the Amana performs poorly — just that there's no third-party confirmation either way. Friedrich's data is more detailed but genuinely mixed.

The CPSC's 2021 New Widetech recall covered roughly 2 million dehumidifiers across about 20 brand names after more than 100 reports of overheating and fires. Both Amana and Friedrich were on the list, but only for units made before September 1, 2017, with older model numbers.

items: **Amana recalled models** included the D930M, D935M, D945E, D950EP, D965E, D970EP and related numbers. Current Amana models use an AM prefix.
**Friedrich recalled models** included the D25, D50 and D70 families (for example D50BP and D70BP). Current Friedrich models carry B1A or B1B suffixes.
**One catch:** some older Friedrich model names have lingered at retailers, so check the date code on any unit, not just the model name.

items.label: Buy the Amana AMND501AW if…
items.text: you need 50 pints for a large or very damp basement, have a floor drain or don't mind emptying a 16.2-pint bucket, and a one-year warranty is acceptable to you.

items.label: Buy the Friedrich D35B1B if…
items.text: your space is a mid-size room or small basement, there's no floor drain where the moisture is, and you want five years of compressor coverage from a specialist HVAC brand.

items.label: Consider neither if…
items.text: you need 50 pints and a pump in one box. Compare self-draining options in our [pump guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) and larger units in our [50-pint guide](/best/best-50-pint-dehumidifier/).

blocks.text: The **Amana AMND501AW** is the better buy for a big, damp basement with a drain nearby: 50 pints a day, three fan speeds, auto-restart and a large bucket. The **Friedrich D35B1B** earns its premium in a mid-size space with no floor drain, thanks to its built-in pump and five-year sealed-system warranty — though the brand's mixed durability marks on an earlier model are worth weighing against that. Whichever you choose, verify the model number and manufacture date before buying a used or clearance unit.

faqs.q: Which is better, Amana or Friedrich?
faqs.a: For capacity, Amana: its AMND501AW removes 50 pints a day versus 35 for the Friedrich D35B1B. For drainage and warranty, Friedrich wins with a built-in pump and five years of sealed-system coverage. Friedrich also has independent test data for an earlier model, though it scored weaker on durability.

faqs.q: Are Amana and Friedrich dehumidifiers made by the same company?
faqs.a: No. They're unrelated brands. Their only real link is that both names appear in the same 2021 CPSC recall of dehumidifiers built by New Widetech.

faqs.q: Why does the Friedrich cost so much more?
faqs.a: Mostly brand positioning and warranty, plus the pump on the D35B1B. Friedrich is a dedicated HVAC manufacturer and includes a five-year sealed-system warranty, while Amana competes on price with a one-year term.

faqs.q: Are current Amana or Friedrich dehumidifiers recalled?
faqs.a: Not the models compared here. The 2021 recall covered older units made before September 1, 2017, with different model numbers. Always check the date code on a used or clearance unit at CPSC.gov.

faqs.q: Do both have a built-in pump?
faqs.a: No. The Friedrich D35B1B has a built-in condensate pump with up to 15 feet of combined lift. The Amana AMND501AW drains to its 16.2-pint bucket or a gravity hose; Amana's pump-equipped version is a separate model, the AMND501PAW.
